cases.answer: In the 2023 Baj et al. study on ECG-based prediction of new-onset AF, random undersampling (RUS) did not improve discrimination in any model and instead worsened calibration: balancing the training set raised ICI values substantially, strongly for XGB and LR (ICI between 0.30 and 0.35 across sample sizes, or growing linearly from 0.01 to 0.3 as event fraction increased) and slightly less for the CNN (ICI 0.1–0.2, or 0.01 to 0.15). At the original event ratio (no imbalance correction, largest sample of 150,000 ECGs), XGB had the lowest ICI at 0.008 (95% CI 0.006–0.01), versus 0.014 for both CNN and LR.

claims.claim: RUS did not improve discrimination and its main effect was to worsen calibration
claims.quote: Balancing the training set with random undersampling did not improve discrimination in any of the models. Instead, the main effect of imbalance corrections was to worsen the models’ calibration

claims.claim: With RUS balancing, ICI rose to 0.30–0.35 for XGB and LR and 0.1–0.2 for CNN
claims.quote: When RUS is applied to balance the training set (Fig. 1D), ICI takes higher values, indicating that models are worse calibrated. The effect is very strong for XGB and LR (ICI values between 0.30 and 0.35 for all the sample sizes considered) and slightly weaker for the CNN model (ICI values between 0.1 and 0.2)

claims.claim: ICI grew linearly with event ratio under RUS (0.01 to 0.3 for XGB/LR, 0.01 to 0.15 for CNN)
claims.quote: increasing the ratio of positive samples with RUS leads to higher values of the ICI, i.e. to less cali- brated models. The effect is very strong for XGB and LR, where ICI values grow linearly from 0.01 to 0.3

claims.claim: At the original event ratio, XGB had the lowest ICI (0.008)
claims.quote: As for the calibration, it can be noticed that there are no substantial differences in the performance of the three models; XGB is the best-performing model with an ICI of 0.008
